title: The Thirteenth Chime
summary: Dusk on Market Hill. Great St Mary's strikes the hour, and then strikes once more. Nobody else seems to hear it.

intro.line: Dusk on Market Hill. The stalls are packing up; Great St Mary's begins to strike the hour.
Eleven. Twelve. Thirteen. The last stroke rings in your teeth, and nobody else so much as looks up.

steps.text: Speak to Nell Tapscott at her flower stall

dialogue.line: You heard that. Don't pretend you didn't; you flinched like a cat at a firework.
The bell struck thirteen. That isn't a thing bells do.
Not ours, no. Not unless something has got into the Concord and started unwinding it.
The old fountain in the middle of the market. Something fell into it on that last stroke. Go and look, quick as you like.

steps.text: Find what fell into the market fountain

dialogue.line: A shard of old bronze lies in the basin, humming the thirteenth stroke over and over.
On the rooftops round the square, something shakes itself loose.

steps.text: Drive off the creatures woken by the chime

dialogue.line: Not bad for somebody who walked into the market for a sandwich.
Take that shard to Pip at the Guildhall steps. Bring a candle-end if you have one. You won't.

steps.text: Take the bell-shard to Pip Hobbe at the Guildhall steps

dialogue.line: Ooh, bronze. Bronze and... sniff... clock oil. Fine oil. Expensive, ticky, nasty oil.
That's the Unwinder's smell. He's been at the market bell. Cracked it right through, and let out what was bound in it.
Whatever's standing up in the middle of the market. Look behind you. No, further. Bigger.

steps.text: Defeat the Bellwarden of Market Hill

intro.line: The Bellwarden of Market Hill wakes: a cracked bronze bell on legs of stone and iron, ringing for blood.

dialogue.line: The Bellwarden folds in on itself with one long, clean note. For the first time tonight, the square is quiet.
Well. That's the first bell answered, and the market still standing. Mostly.
The Concord keeps the Undertide out of this town: bells, clocks, conduits, all of it. Somebody is unpicking it stroke by stroke.
Take this posy. It's charmed, and it's the last of the marigolds. You're a Warden now, whether you like it or not.
Go and find Absalom Crane on the steps of Great St Mary's. He'll want to know his tower struck thirteen.
